title: The Courier Link
topic: Using APIs: HTTP methods, JSON and status codes
briefing: Orders are stored, now they need delivering. SwiftShip, our courier, has an API: a website made for programs instead of people. It speaks JSON. Get delivery quotes, pick the cheapest one that's fast enough, book it, and check on a parcel that's gone missing.
hints: requests.get(url, params={"weight_kg": weight_kg}) adds ?weight_kg=... to the address. resp.status_code tells you whether it worked (200 means OK), and resp.json() turns the JSON into Python lists and dicts.

Filter the quotes with a comprehension (days <= 2), then min(..., key=lambda q: q["price"]). requests.post(url, json={...}) sends data. A 404 status means not found, so check the status before calling .json().

resp = requests.get(RATES_URL, params={"weight_kg": weight_kg}) / quotes = resp.json() / fast = [q for q in quotes if q["days"] <= 2] / best = min(fast, key=lambda q: q["price"]) / booking = requests.post(BOOK_URL, json={"service": best["service"], "weight_kg": weight_kg}) / tracking = booking.json()["tracking"] / lost = requests.get(TRACK_URL + lost_parcel) / parcel_status = lost.json()["status"] if lost.status_code == 200 else "not found"
bonus: Loop over several weights (1, 5, 20 kg) and print the cheapest quote for each one.
